title: SPLENDID (Spleen stiffness, liver stiffness and body composition for prognostic stratification in liver Disease)
summary: In advanced liver disease, known as liver cirrhosis, the condition of the liver can suddenly worsen. Doctors use various blood values to estimate how patients will fare in the coming days. However, these methods are not always sufficient. This study therefore investigates whether two new, painless measurement methods can help predict the course of the disease at an earlier stage. One method measures the stiffness of the liver and spleen using ultrasound, while the other determines body composition, particularly water content, using a special body scale. During the hospital stay, these measurements are performed twice: once within the first three days after admission and again four to seven days later. Approximately one and three months after discharge, a brief telephone follow-up is conducted to assess the patient's health status. Participation is voluntary and can be withdrawn at any time without disadvantage.

interventions.name: Timepoint 1 (Baseline): Within 72 hours of unplanned hospital admission, liver and spleen stiffness are measured by transient elastography (FibroScan®), and body composition parameters are assessed by bioimpedance analysis. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Unplanned hospital admission to a general ward
- Confirmed diagnosis of decompensated liver cirrhosis or acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) according to clinical criteria
- Written informed consent for study participation
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of capacity to consent
- Missing written informed consent
- Need for monitoring or intensive care treatment (treatment in an intensive care or intermediate care unit)
- Inability to be transported within the hospital
- Inability to stand up independently for the bioimpedance measurement and to remain standing without assistance for the duration of the measurement
- Clinical condition that does not allow safe performance of the examinations
- Technical infeasibility of elastography measurement
- Participation in another interventional study
